title: Wi-Fi is short for Wireless Fidelity.
description:
Wi-Fi is short for Wireless Fidelity. The dictionary calls that reading spurious. Phil Belanger, who ran the naming, is blunter: it is not an acronym, and there is no meaning.

The alliance behind the new 802.11b radio could not market "IEEE 802.11b Direct Sequence," so it hired the agency that had named Prozac and Compaq. What came back was Wi-Fi, a pun on hi-fi, chosen from a list of ten.

The name was chosen first. The meaning was bolted on. Some board members could not stomach a name that explained nothing, so they added the tag line "The Standard for Wireless Fidelity." It ran about a year, then was quietly retired.

The group never wrote a standard. It certifies that devices interoperate; the standard is IEEE's. So the phrase is wrong on both words, Belanger's own verdict is that it only diluted the brand.

The man who picked the name spent years asking people to forget the tag line.
